headline: High: Rasa can exfiltrate conversation text to allowlisted channels while the paired awesome-list profile adds no protective boundary, creating default leakage and cascading-action risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no I/O surfaces and no runnable path, so it cannot inject B directly. B ingests text/voice and calls external chat APIs, so prompt-like content could arrive only through manual or channel-mediated copy. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so the pathway is limited and not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-derived text into a B channel or connector
IF B is configured to treat inbound messages as instructions
mitigations: Disable any manual copy-paste bridge between A outputs and B inputs
Add a fixed system prompt in B that ignores embedded instructions in user text
Require human review before forwarding A-derived content into B
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to messages before B processes them

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, so it is not a leakage source. B handles text/voice and can send data to allowlisted APIs, but the pair shows no shared workspace or sensitive classes. Leakage is therefore limited to ordinary conversational content entering B, not a documented cross-agent spill.
conditions: IF A-derived content includes sensitive text and is forwarded into B
IF B connectors are configured to transmit conversation content to external services
mitigations: Keep A outputs free of secrets or personal data
Restrict B connectors to the minimum allowlisted channels
Turn off transcript logging in B where available
Review outbound message templates before enabling them
requires-engineering: segregate A and B into separate workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, network, or mutable-resource permissions, while B supports multiple instances false and exposes only chat API connectors. There is no documented overlapping write surface such as filesystem, git, or shared OAuth scopes, so direct capability conflict is unlikely and any contention would require extra orchestration not shown here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents the same mutable resource
IF B is extended with write access to a shared store
mitigations: Avoid assigning both agents the same mutable target
Run B as a single instance only
Document ownership of any shared resource
requires-engineering: add locking around shared writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can supply curated content, and B is a dialogue agent that may treat inbound text as authoritative unless prompted otherwise. Because B connects to external messaging channels, a mistaken A-derived recommendation can cascade into user-facing responses. The pair lacks a verification step in the profiles, so the interaction exists in default conversational workflows.
conditions: IF A-derived text is forwarded into B without verification
IF B is allowed to answer users directly from that text
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before B replies
Mark A outputs as untrusted reference material
Constrain B to summarize rather than execute recommendations
requires-engineering: add citation checks before B sends messages

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source awesome-list with no touched data classes, so it presents no residency or retention issue on its own. B handles text and voice and may route them through allowlisted third-party channels, but the profiles do not show regulated data classes or a specific jurisdiction mismatch. The compliance risk is therefore limited and not directly evidenced for the pair.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is sent through B connectors
IF the deployment requires a residency or retention policy not enforced by B
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through B
Confirm connector retention settings before enabling them
Keep A as a non-data-bearing reference repo
requires-engineering: document jurisdiction and retention controls
